pages.text: <!doctype html> Home | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Orthopedic and sports medicine care in Chicago Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine treats injuries and joint conditions for adults and young athletes across Chicago and the western suburbs. Our surgeons and physical therapists work in the same building, so the person who plans your surgery is the person who follows your recovery. What we treat Knee Replacement ACL Reconstruction Rotator Cuff Repair Sports Injury Care Joint Injections Hand and Wrist Surgery We also publish plain-language explanations of the two areas patients ask about most: sports medicine and joint replacement. Our team has cared for the region's athletes and working adults for over twenty years of experience in orthopedic practice. We accept most major insurance plans and offer early morning appointments for patients who cannot miss a work day. pages.title: Our Team | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.description: Meet the orthopedic surgeons and therapists
pages.text: <!doctype html> Our Team | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Our Team Every surgeon at Northbank is fellowship trained, and every therapist on our staff works only with orthopedic and sports medicine patients. We keep the team small on purpose: you should be able to reach the person who treated you. Dr. Alina Reyes, MD Dr. Alina Reyes, MD is a board-certified orthopedic surgeon who completed her sports medicine fellowship in Chicago. She treats knee and shoulder injuries and serves as a team physician for two local high schools. She has practiced in Chicago for fourteen years and speaks English and Spanish. Dr. Marcus Whitfield, MD Dr. Marcus Whitfield, MD is a board-certified orthopedic surgeon focused on joint replacement of the hip and knee. He completed his residency and adult reconstruction fellowship in the Midwest and has performed joint replacement surgery for eighteen years. He sees patients at both clinics. Physical therapy team Our therapists are licensed doctors of physical therapy and see patients in the same building as the surgical team. Coordinating both under one roof shortens the gap between an operation and the first rehabilitation session, which is the part of recovery patients most often ask about. pages.title: FAQ | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
headings: Do I need a referral to be seen?
How long will I wait for an appointment?
Can I see the same surgeon at both clinics?
What should I bring to the first visit?
pages.text: <!doctype html> FAQ | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Frequently Asked Questions Do I need a referral to be seen? Most plans allow you to book directly with an orthopedic specialist. A few require a referral from your primary care physician first. Our staff check when you call so you are not turned away at the desk. How long will I wait for an appointment? Routine appointments are usually within two weeks. Acute sports injuries are seen within the same week during the season, and we hold slots open for that purpose. Will I need surgery? Most patients we see do not. Injections, therapy and time resolve the majority of orthopedic problems. We will tell you plainly when an operation is the better option and when it is not. Can I see the same surgeon at both clinics? Yes. Our surgeons see patients at both the River North and Oak Park clinics, and you can choose whichever is easier to reach. What should I bring to the first visit? Bring your insurance card, any imaging you have already had, a list of your medications, and shorts if the problem is in your knee or hip. pages.title: Knee Replacement | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.text: <!doctype html> Knee Replacement | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Knee Replacement Knee replacement is an operation for a knee joint whose cartilage has worn away, usually from osteoarthritis. When the cartilage is gone, the bones move against each other, and the pain typically arrives first with stairs and long walks and later at rest. We recommend the operation only after bracing, therapy and injections have been tried and the joint still limits daily life. What the procedure involves During the procedure the worn surfaces of the thigh bone and shin bone are removed and replaced with a metal and plastic implant sized to your anatomy. The implant is positioned with the leg aligned so that load passes through the joint the way it did before the cartilage wore down. Most operations take about ninety minutes and use a spinal anaesthetic with sedation rather than general anaesthesia. Who it suits Recovery begins the same day. A physical therapist has most patients standing within a few hours and walking with a frame before discharge. The first six weeks are the working part of recovery: bending the knee, rebuilding the quadriceps, and walking further each week. Most people return to driving between four and six weeks and to low-impact activity by three months. Recovery and follow-up We follow every knee replacement for a year with scheduled reviews at six weeks, three months and twelve months. Bring the walking aid you are using to each visit so we can see how your gait is changing rather than asking you to describe it. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: ACL Reconstruction | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.description: ACL reconstruction and return to sport
pages.text: <!doctype html> ACL Reconstruction | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact ACL Reconstruction The anterior cruciate ligament stabilises the knee against twisting. It tears most often in sport, when a planted foot turns while the body keeps moving. People usually describe a pop, immediate swelling, and a knee that feels as though it will give way on turning. What the procedure involves Reconstruction replaces the torn ligament with a graft, most commonly taken from the hamstring or the patellar tendon. The graft is passed through tunnels drilled in the thigh bone and shin bone and fixed at the same angle as the original ligament. It is keyhole surgery and a day case: patients go home the same afternoon. Who it suits The rehabilitation matters more than the operation. For the first two weeks the priority is swelling and full extension. Strength work follows, then running at around three months, then changing direction. Return to competitive sport is normally between nine and twelve months, and we test rather than guess: we compare the operated and non-operated leg before clearing anyone. Recovery and follow-up Younger athletes tear the ligament again more often than older patients, which is why we do not shorten the programme for people who feel ready early. The graft takes the same amount of time to mature regardless of how strong the leg feels. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: Rotator Cuff Repair | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.description: Rotator cuff repair for shoulder tears
pages.text: <!doctype html> Rotator Cuff Repair | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Rotator Cuff Repair The rotator cuff is the group of four tendons that hold the shoulder in its socket and lift the arm. Tears develop either suddenly, from a fall onto an outstretched arm, or gradually with age as the tendon frays. The typical complaint is pain reaching overhead and pain lying on that shoulder at night. What the procedure involves Not every tear needs surgery. Small degenerative tears often settle with a structured therapy programme and a corticosteroid injection. We advise repair when a tear is full thickness, when weakness rather than pain is the main problem, or when a good therapy programme has not changed matters after three months. Who it suits The repair is done arthroscopically. Small anchors are placed into the bone and the tendon is drawn back to its footprint on the humerus with sutures. Patients go home the same day in a sling, which stays on for four to six weeks to protect the repair while the tendon heals to bone. Recovery and follow-up Shoulder recovery is slower than knee recovery and it is worth knowing that in advance. Passive movement starts within the first fortnight, active movement at six weeks, and strengthening at three months. Most people are comfortable at four months and at their best at nine to twelve. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: Sports Injury Care | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.text: <!doctype html> Sports Injury Care | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Sports Injury Care We see athletes at every level, from professionals to adults who play once a week. Most sports injuries are not surgical: sprains, muscle strains, tendon overload and stress reactions make up the majority of what walks through the door, and they respond to accurate diagnosis and a graded loading programme rather than an operation. What the procedure involves Same-week appointments are held open for acute injuries during the season. If you are injured on a Saturday, call on Monday and you will be seen that week rather than in a month. Imaging is arranged in the same building when it changes the plan and skipped when it does not. Who it suits For young athletes we look at training load as well as the injured part. A stress injury in a fifteen year old who has just moved from one sport to three is a workload problem wearing the costume of an ankle problem, and treating only the ankle sends them back to the same place. Recovery and follow-up Our therapists build return-to-play programmes with the athlete's coach where the athlete wants us to. Clearing someone to train is a different decision from clearing them to compete, and we make both explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: Joint Injections | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.text: <!doctype html> Joint Injections | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Joint Injections An injection is a way of putting medication exactly where the problem is instead of asking the whole body to carry it. We use them for arthritic joints, inflamed tendons and bursae, both to reduce pain and, when the diagnosis is uncertain, to confirm which structure is responsible. What the procedure involves Corticosteroid injections reduce inflammation and typically give relief measured in weeks to months. Hyaluronic acid injections are used in some arthritic knees. Platelet-rich plasma is prepared from your own blood and used for selected tendon problems. We will tell you which of these has good evidence for your specific condition and which does not. Who it suits Nearly all of our injections are given under ultrasound guidance in the clinic. Guidance means the needle goes where it was intended to go, which matters most in the shoulder and the hip where landmarks alone are unreliable. The appointment takes about twenty minutes. Recovery and follow-up An injection is a way to make rehabilitation possible, not a substitute for it. We book the therapy appointment at the same time as the injection so the window of reduced pain is used for the strengthening work that changes the underlying problem. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: Hand and Wrist Surgery | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.description: Hand and wrist surgery and therapy
pages.text: <!doctype html> Hand and Wrist Surgery | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Hand and Wrist Surgery The hand is the part of the body people notice the fastest when it stops working. We treat carpal tunnel syndrome, trigger finger, thumb base arthritis, ganglion cysts and fractures of the wrist and fingers, in both working adults and retired patients. What the procedure involves Carpal tunnel release is our most common hand operation. It is done under local anaesthetic with the patient awake, takes about fifteen minutes, and relieves the night-time numbness that brings most people in. Office workers are typically back at a keyboard within two weeks and manual workers within six. Who it suits Trigger finger and thumb base arthritis are often treated without surgery first, with a splint and an injection. When surgery is needed for thumb base arthritis it is a larger operation than patients expect, with a recovery measured in months rather than weeks, and we would rather say that at the first appointment than at the follow-up. Recovery and follow-up Hand therapy is part of the treatment rather than an optional extra. Our hand therapists see patients in the same building, and for fracture and tendon work the therapy programme starts within days of the operation. Individual results vary, and every procedure on this page carries risks and limitations that we discuss with you before you decide. pages.title: Sports Medicine | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.text: <!doctype html> Sports Medicine | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Sports Medicine Sports medicine is the part of orthopedics concerned with keeping active people active. This page explains how we think about training load, why most injuries in recreational athletes are overuse rather than accident, and what a graded return to play actually involves week by week. An overuse injury is a mismatch between what tissue can tolerate and what it is being asked to do. The tissue is rarely abnormal; the load curve is. That is why the first question we ask about a sore Achilles is not what it feels like but what changed in the six weeks before it started hurting. Graded return to play means adding one variable at a time: volume, then intensity, then change of direction, then contact. Adding two at once is how an athlete who felt ready ends up back at the start. We write the progression down so the athlete and the coach are reading the same plan. pages.title: Joint Replacement | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine
pages.text: <!doctype html> Joint Replacement | Northbank Orthopedic & Sports Medicine Home Services Our Team Insurance FAQ Reviews Contact Joint Replacement Joint replacement is an option when arthritis has worn a joint to the point that it dictates the shape of your day. This page describes how we decide the timing with you, and what the first year after a hip or knee replacement typically looks like. Timing is a conversation, not a threshold. Radiographs correlate poorly with how much a joint bothers a particular person, so we ask about stairs, sleep and distance rather than reading a number off an image. A joint that stops you sleeping is a stronger argument than a joint that looks worse. The first year has a shape. Weeks one to six are about movement and swelling. Months two and three are about strength and walking distance. Months four to twelve are quieter, and most of the remaining improvement happens without you noticing it happening.
